subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle model as a static structure without joints, since it's not a creature requiring a skeleton, and starting to work out the truck's dimensions.

Now I'm sketching the specific parts: a 7m-long armored truck with six big wheels, an angular cab, cargo bed armor plating, roof turret, light bars, antenna, missile pods, sensor dome, and exhaust stacks, planning to build it with box and cylinder primitives plus kit helpers for paneled metal paint and glow effects, and SVG textures for emblem decals, warning stripes, and screen graphics. I'm working out wheel placement and ground-level coordinates next.

Now I'm working out the cab geometry, figuring out rotation angles and extrusion axes so the side profile extrudes correctly along the right plane.

I'm plotting the cab outline points in (z,y) coordinates — low sloped hood front, angled windshield, flat roof, vertical back — then extruding that profile to a thickness of 2.0 centered on x. I'm planning the windshield as a separate slanted box fitted between the hood-top and roof-front points.

Working out the box rotation for the windshield...

Now I'm placing the windshield texture plane with reflections and HUD lines, then adding side windows as dark angled planes on the cab sides and armored slit windows as small dark boxes, before moving on to hood details.

Adding front grille, glow headlights, roof light bar, and a wedge bull bar with warning stripe, plus wheel arch fenders and armor skirt plates between the axles.

Then I'm designing the cargo module as a hardened military compartment with ribbed armor panels, chamfered top edges, glowing bottom strips, a rear door with emblem, and ammo racks, topped with a turret ring carrying twin barrels and a sensor, missile pods with 2x3 tube arrays, a radar dish, and glowing-tipped antenna rods.

Now I'm detailing the roof accessories (light bar, drone, satellite), dual exhaust stacks with heat glow rings behind the cab, and the underbody with chassis rails, axles, differentials, suspension springs, drive shaft, fuel tanks, and magenta underglow strips, while settling on a cyberpunk palette of gunmetal, magenta, cyan, and warning yellow applied through paneled metal paint.

I'm realizing the paint texel density won't resolve thin seams at this scale, so I'm writing a custom armor paint function with thin grid lines, camo-like noise mottling, warm top lighting, dark undersides, and mud buildup near the bottom.

Now I'm planning the parts budget (~200) and sketching helper loops, plus the texture set: a hex/skull decal for the cargo side, yellow-black warning stripes for the bumper, a dark grille with cyan accent lines, and windshield glass, while skipping a HUD screen for now.

I'm also planning plate text ("MX-2077"), a brand-safe neon sign reading "NOMAD-77" in monospace, a hex-chevron side decal, and tire tread textures using cylindrical UV mapping with chevron patterns tinted dark, noting glow effects can apply to both textured and flat-colored parts.

Now I'm setting up the builder with a 2048px paint size and writing helper functions for boxes and cylinders, handling directional axes for cylinder orientation, then placing tires and wheel hubs at each axle position along the truck's length.

Deciding to skip complex tread texturing and just use a dark flat color for the tires and hubs instead, keeping things simple for now.

Now I'm sketching the chassis frame: two side rails as thin boxes running the length of the car, positioned at the axle height with wheels radius 0.62.

Checking for overlaps between the cab, cargo body, and tires—bumping the cargo bottom up to around y1.35 to clear the tire tops and avoid intersecting the rails near the front wheel position.

Now I'm working out fender geometry to cover the wheel arches, placing flared boxes above each tire and adding a side skirt plate to bridge the gap between the cab width and the wider fender footprint.

I'm also finalizing the cab body profile points for the hood and windshield slope, computing the windshield's tilt angle and offsetting the surface normal slightly to give it thickness, then planning to add hood vents along the sloped top.

Now I'm positioning the exhaust stacks near the cab's rear sides, checking they clear the cargo box's z-range and sit flush against the cab without colliding, then starting to define the cargo body's main box dimensions and center position.

For the top edges, I'm considering adding chamfered corner plates using 45°-rotated boxes to give a beveled armored look at the cargo box's top corners, rather than trying to carve actual chamfers. I'm also starting to lay out side ribs along the cargo box using a loop of small boxes for added surface detail.

Now I'm adding more cosmetic details: vent grills, side emblem plates, a cyan neon strip glow along the sides, and magenta underglow strips near the bottom. At the rear I'm planning door panels with hinge bars, a hazard plate, and a text plate reading something like "HEAVY HAULER."

Then I'm working on taillights as glowing red boxes, a rear bumper with warning texture, and a tow hook. On top of the cargo roof I'm designing a turret assembly with a rotating ring, body box, cupola, twin barrels with shrouds and muzzle brakes, a sensor ball with a glowing cyan eye, an ammo box, and a hatch.

Now I'm figuring out missile pod placement on the rear roof, angling them upward and forward using directional vectors, and setting up the box and tube geometry with proper orientation math to align each pod correctly in 3D space.

I'm adding the launch tubes with dark exteriors and glowing warhead tips inside each pod, then moving on to designing the radar dish mounted on a mast using a lathe-generated profile for the dish shape.

For the cab, I'm sketching roof details: a light bar with alternating cyan/magenta glow segments, antennas with glowing tips, side mirrors on arms, and thin door line details.

I'm working out window placement along the slanted front pillar, calculating where the glass pane sits on the sloped surface so it fits within the roofline without clipping.

Now I'm adding hull armor details: a wedge-shaped hood plate, bolted side armor boxes, slim glowing headlight boxes positioned near the front corners, and a recessed grille panel between them sized to fit the headlight spacing, plus a bumper box below.

Working through the plow blade geometry now, defining its wedge-shaped side profile with dark coloring and a yellow edge, then adjusting overall vehicle length and repositioning the front and rear wheel z-coordinates to match.

Still laying out mechanical components: axle cylinders and differential sphere at the centerline, leaf spring suspension boxes near each axle, tilted shock cylinders, a drive shaft running between axles, and fuel tank cylinders positioned between the front and rear axles.

Working out the gap between front and rear tire positions to size and place the fuel tanks correctly, then adding straps and considering a protective cage. I also need to position the wheel hub textures and sketch a rear fender/mudguard box large enough to cover both rear dual wheels.

Checking that the rear fender clears the cargo body bottom and tires, then adding side mud plates near the outer tire edges and matching front fender dimensions at the corresponding z-range. I'm also planning body side skirts between the cab and cargo area, including cargo bottom skirts for extra coverage.

Now I'm designing the paint shader for the armor: blending base and dark tones using noise for mottled camo, shifting toward a cooler bluish tint on upward-facing surfaces, darkening the underside, adding a seam grid based on dominant surface axis, and mixing in a muddy brown tone near the lower sections based on height.

I'm setting up the color palette: a dark steel-teal armor with camo variants, plus flat accent colors like magenta, cyan, yellow, black, steel, and red, keeping the total under the flat color limit.

Writing emblem SVG texture...

Still designing icon elements...

I'm mapping out the remaining ten textures—hub bolts, tail plate, side glass, cargo holo screen, and signage—then planning to write the TypeScript carefully with minimal typing and a simple vector type alias.

Setting up imports and part helper functions...

Still writing armor paint logic...

Writing tire paint logic...

Now building the chassis structure: steel box frame members, cross members at several z positions, and a belly armor plate positioned above where a drive shaft would sit.

Still writing axle components...

Now building the cab extrusion from the outline shape with sharp beveled corners, then adding a roof armor plate on top.

Adding door armor slabs, seam lines, and window frames with slightly recessed glass panes for the cab sides...

Still placing hood vents...

Adding exhaust caps and heat glow rings, then moving to bumper, plow, and cargo details like armor paneling, ribs, corner castings, vent fans, and glowing side screen panels.

I'm placing a glowing neon "2077" roof banner above the cab for visual flair, and adding magenta underglow strips along the chassis between the wheel wells to give the vehicle that cyberpunk lighting feel.

Now I'm adding details like a tow hitch, whip antennas with glowing tips at the cargo corners, and estimating the part count stays manageable. I'm also starting on a lathe-generated radar dish shape for the roof, defining its cross-section profile to create the curved satellite dish geometry.

Computing orientation quaternions for the pods and tubes...

That checks out roughly, so I'll add a bridging support block. With planning settled, I'm ready to write the final code: defining armor color materials for a teal-grey cab and olive cargo body for contrast, then positioning the windshield plane with the right size, offset, and angled orientation.

For wheels, I'm sizing hub planes and offsetting them outside the tire radius, then reasoning that the tire's end caps will hide the rim entirely so I just rely on the hub plane plus a small protruding hub cap cylinder for detail.
